A data structure for empty-space skipping in pre-integrated volume rendering.
It modifies the region covered by each block so that each block covers some region of which thickness is at least the sampling distance.
To skip a line segment formed by two sampling points, test only the single block that contains the line segment (or overlaps it sufficiently) to determine if it is transparent.

- **Time Complexity:** The object-order skipping phase is $O(1)$ per pixel for depth range computation (via rasterization) and $O(N)$ for ray casting, where $N$ is the number of samples in the active range.
The per-sample check for image-order skipping is $O(1)$.
- **Measured Performance:** The method reduces overhead by skipping most empty space with no cost using modified ray segments.
Simple to implement with standard GPU rasterization features.
- **Limitations:** Inactive blocks enclosed by active blocks are not excluded from the search range, leading to per-sample checks.
- **When to Use:** Suitable for sparse volumes with clear isosurfaces or transparent regions.
